deepmerge
Copyright (c) 2012 James Halliday, Josh Duff, and other contributors
- File packages/apidom-core/src/deepmerge.ts contains algorithms that we originally created
  in https://github.com/TehShrike/deepmerge/blob/master/index.js to handle deep merging of JavaScript Objects and Arrays.
  These algorithms have been reverse engineered and adapted to support deep merging of ApiDOM structures.
- File packages/apidom-core/test/deepmerge.ts contains tests and fixtures that were originally created
  in https://github.com/TehShrike/deepmerge/blob/master/test/merge.js to test deep merging of JavaScript Objects and Arrays.
  These tests have been adapted to support testing deep merging of ApiDOM structures.
- File packages/apidom-core/README.md contains text fragments that were originally created
  in https://github.com/TehShrike/deepmerge/blob/master/readme.md to document deepmerge library.
  These text fragments have been amended to describe merging of ApiDOM structures.
Copy of the MIT license can be found in `LICENSES/MIT.txt` file.

=== argparse@2.0.1 ===
License: Python-2.0
Homepage: https://github.com/nodeca/argparse
License-Text-Source: bundled file

A. HISTORY OF THE SOFTWARE
==========================

Python was created in the early 1990s by Guido van Rossum at Stichting
Mathematisch Centrum (CWI, see http://www.cwi.nl) in the Netherlands
as a successor of a language called ABC.  Guido remains Python's
principal author, although it includes many contributions from others.

In 1995, Guido continued his work on Python at the Corporation for
National Research Initiatives (CNRI, see http://www.cnri.reston.va.us)
in Reston, Virginia where he released several versions of the
software.

In May 2000, Guido and the Python core development team moved to
BeOpen.com to form the BeOpen PythonLabs team.  In October of the same
year, the PythonLabs team moved to Digital Creations, which became
Zope Corporation.  In 2001, the Python Software Foundation (PSF, see
https://www.python.org/psf/) was formed, a non-profit organization
created specifically to own Python-related Intellectual Property.
Zope Corporation was a sponsoring member of the PSF.

All Python releases are Open Source (see http://www.opensource.org for
the Open Source Definition).  Historically, most, but not all, Python
releases have also been GPL-compatible; the table below summarizes
the various releases.

    Release         Derived     Year        Owner       GPL-
                    from                                compatible? (1)

    0.9.0 thru 1.2              1991-1995   CWI         yes
    1.3 thru 1.5.2  1.2         1995-1999   CNRI        yes
    1.6             1.5.2       2000        CNRI        no
    2.0             1.6         2000        BeOpen.com  no
    1.6.1           1.6         2001        CNRI        yes (2)
    2.1             2.0+1.6.1   2001        PSF         no
    2.0.1           2.0+1.6.1   2001        PSF         yes
    2.1.1           2.1+2.0.1   2001        PSF         yes
    2.1.2           2.1.1       2002        PSF         yes
    2.1.3           2.1.2       2002        PSF         yes
    2.2 and above   2.1.1       2001-now    PSF         yes

Footnotes:

(1) GPL-compatible doesn't mean that we're distributing Python under
    the GPL.  All Python licenses, unlike the GPL, let you distribute
    a modified version without making your changes open source.  The
    GPL-compatible licenses make it possible to combine Python with
    other software that is released under the GPL; the others don't.

(2) According to Richard Stallman, 1.6.1 is not GPL-compatible,
    because its license has a choice of law clause.  According to
    CNRI, however, Stallman's lawyer has told CNRI's lawyer that 1.6.1
    is "not incompatible" with the GPL.

Thanks to the many outside volunteers who have worked under Guido's
direction to make these releases possible.

SECTION B — Python dependencies (device-executor)
=================================================

The device-executor image (services/proxy/src/device-executor) is a Python
component whose deps come from its requirements.txt, NOT from npm. They ship in
the device-executor image (FastAPI service on :8190 that drives network devices
via netmiko/napalm/impacket/pywinrm/pyghmi).

This committed file is a hand-curated register of the DIRECT requirements with
their upstream-declared SPDX ids and PyPI URLs. The AUTHORITATIVE full license
text (direct + all transitive deps) is regenerated at image build time by
`pip-licenses` — see services/proxy/src/device-executor/Dockerfile and the
regen helper scripts/licenses/regen-python.sh. Refresh this file whenever
requirements.txt changes:

    bash scripts/licenses/regen-python.sh   # builds the image, runs pip-licenses

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Direct requirements (services/proxy/src/device-executor/requirements.txt)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Name                          Version spec     License (declared)   PyPI
fastapi                       >=0.110.0        MIT                 https://pypi.org/project/fastapi
uvicorn                       >=0.29.0         BSD-3-Clause        https://pypi.org/project/uvicorn
pywinrm                       >=0.4.3          MIT                 https://pypi.org/project/pywinrm
impacket                      ==0.13.0         Apache-2.0(*)       https://pypi.org/project/impacket
napalm                        >=5.0.0          Apache-2.0          https://pypi.org/project/napalm
netmiko                       >=4.4.0          MIT                 https://pypi.org/project/netmiko
pyghmi                        >=1.6.0          Apache-2.0          https://pypi.org/project/pyghmi
napalm-huawei-vrp             >=1.2.0          Apache-2.0(*)       https://pypi.org/project/napalm-huawei-vrp
napalm-h3c-comware            >=0.1.5          Apache-2.0(*)       https://pypi.org/project/napalm-h3c-comware
napalm-procurve               >=0.6.0          Apache-2.0(*)       https://pypi.org/project/napalm-procurve
napalm-s350                   >=0.5.1          Apache-2.0(*)       https://pypi.org/project/napalm-s350
napalm-ruckus-fastiron        >=1.0.26         Apache-2.0(*)       https://pypi.org/project/napalm-ruckus-fastiron
napalm-dlink                  >=0.1.0          Apache-2.0(*)       https://pypi.org/project/napalm-dlink

(*) Community NAPALM drivers / impacket occasionally declare a different
    permissive id (Apache-2.0 vs MIT vs BSD). Confirm the definitive id and full
    text via `pip-licenses` in the built image or on the PyPI page linked above.
    The build-time pip-licenses output (the authoritative version written into
    the device-executor image at /app/THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt) is the source of
    truth — this committed register is a human-reviewable baseline.

Notable transitive deps that will appear in the build-time output (sample):
  paramiko (LGPL-2.1-or-later) — pulled by netmiko/napalm; LGPL obligations apply
  (ship source/object + prominent notice). See pip-licenses output in-image.

SECTION C — Vendored binaries (OpenTofu + Terraform/OpenTofu providers)
========================================================================

The device-executor image (services/proxy/src/device-executor) ships pre-built,
offline binaries whose licenses are NOT npm/pip packages and so are not covered
by Section A/B. They are vendored at image build time and never downloaded at
runtime (fully offline delivery).

License ids below are the upstream-declared SPDX ids. The canonical LICENSE text
for each provider ALSO ships inside the image's vendored plugin mirror at
/opt/tofu-plugins/<registry>/<namespace>/<name>/<version>/LICENSE — confirm there
or via the upstream registry URL if ever in doubt. Provider versions mirror
services/proxy/src/device-executor/providers.tf; keep this file in sync when
providers.tf pins change.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Version:  1.9.0  (ARG OPENTOFU_VERSION in the device-executor Dockerfile)

URL:      https://opentofu.org
Full license text (MPL-2.0): see the MPL-2.0 block in scripts/licenses/spdx-texts.txt,
              or https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/
